hotspots.whyItMatters: Cat 3/Cat 5-era category distinctions still anchor 'what wire for what job' questions on the low-voltage side.
hotspots.cite: Telecommunication Wiring. Confirm chapter in your copy. Cross-check NEC Article 800
hotspots.trap: Treating category rating as only about speed and ignoring that it also governs required physical handling (bend radius, untwist length) needed to preserve performance.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Punch-down and termination workmanship rules are a recurring low-voltage installation topic.
hotspots.cite: Telecommunication Wiring. Confirm chapter in your copy
hotspots.trap: Over-untwisting pairs at the termination point, which degrades performance even on an otherwise correct run.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Physical separation between telecom/low-voltage and power conductors prevents induced noise.
hotspots.cite: Telecommunication Wiring. Confirm chapter in your copy. Cross-check NEC 800.133
hotspots.trap: Assuming any conduit or raceway separation 'looks fine' without checking the specific minimum-spacing rule for parallel runs near power conductors.
